notes: Similarity = 100 / (1 + D), D = sum(w_i d_i) / sum(w_i) over COMPARABLE features only. It is a heuristic index, not a validated probability.

Numeric features are compared at a HARMONISED ~3.7 km baseline: Earth 90 m DEMs are block-averaged to the MOLA MEGDR 16 ppd cell size before slope and roughness are computed, so both planets' terrain statistics describe the same physical scale.
Landing suitability and environmental similarity are separate calculations and never feed each other.

features.label: Regional slope (median, ~3.7 km baseline)
features.rationale: Terrain gradient at the same baseline on both planets. Scale of 1.5 deg means a 1.5 deg difference contributes d = 1.

features.label: Detrended relief (~3.7 km cells)
features.rationale: Plane-removed elevation standard deviation across the footprint at a harmonised cell size. Scale 100 m.

features.label: Terrain morphology
features.rationale: Categorical tags (e.g. impact_crater, lava_plain, playa, alluvial_fan, permafrost). Distance = 1 - |A and B| / |A or B|. Tags are literature-sourced and listed per site.

features.label: Mineralogy / composition
features.rationale: Categorical composition tags from cited literature (e.g. basalt, clays, sulfates, carbonates, evaporites). Same Jaccard distance.

features.label: Aridity (mean precipitation)
features.rationale: Mars has no liquid precipitation (value 0, physical fact, source: literature). Earth values are NASA POWER climatology. Lower Earth precipitation = better aridity analog. Scale 1 mm/day.

features.label: Top-of-atmosphere insolation (annual mean)
features.rationale: Computed identically for both planets, but dominated by heliocentric distance rather than site character, so it is informational (default weight 0) and disclosed rather than matched on.

noncomparable_disclosures: Atmospheric pressure: Mars surface pressure is ~0.6 kPa (about 0.6% of Earth's 101 kPa); no Earth site is comparable.
Gravity: Mars surface gravity is 3.71 m/s2 versus Earth's 9.81 m/s2.
Radiation: Mars has no global magnetic field and a thin atmosphere, so surface radiation dose is far higher than anywhere on Earth.
Temperature: Mars mean surface temperatures are far below any Earth analog; thermal comparisons are qualitative only.
Elevation datum: Mars elevations are relative to the MOLA areoid (GMM3), Earth elevations to the EGM2008 geoid; absolute elevations are therefore shown but never differenced.
